div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: the pool — each backend gets the concurrency it can use

p.b: five failure modes, each handled where it can be

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a dead worker → BrokenProcessPool
results collected with as_completed, not map,
so documents that already finished are kept

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a hung pool → stall watchdog
fires when no document completes for stall_timeout;
warns at half. Not a per-document deadline — no threshold
separates a hang from the legitimate 246s document.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a slow document → document_timeout
a real kill for pdftotext; a cooperative between-stages
check for docling. Not equally strong, and said so.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CUDA OOM → demote that worker to CPU
for the rest of the run, and retry immediately.
Surviving the CPU retry marks it transient.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Ctrl+C → explicit SIGINT handler
except KeyboardInterrupt around as_completed()
never fires. Terminate, grace, kill(), os._exit —
safe only because the ledger commits incrementally.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

p.b: the ceiling is the host's, not the request's

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
allowed_cpus() = len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))
the CPUs this process may run on — not os.cpu_count().
On the dev machine those are 48 and 96.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
one worker was measured holding ~300% CPU.
A later full-corpus sweep found the divisor
too conservative by ~1.41x — not yet changed.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
silently obeying thrashes; silently ignoring leaves
someone believing they configured something they didn't

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
forkserver begins importing torch + docling
in the background — and declines outright when
no pool is coming (pdftotext, or workers = 1)

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
read bibliography.bib — ~2.5s
deliberately started after the pre-start, so the
import overlaps the read: a fixed ~1.5-2s saved

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small: which documents actually need a parse

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
a genuinely different code path: no executor,
no pickling, no subprocess. Incremental skipping
means a routine run has almost nothing to do,
so pool setup would cost more than it saves.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ThreadPoolExecutor · pdftotext
external subprocess — releases the GIL.
Processes would add pickling and spawn cost
to buy the same OS-level concurrency.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ProcessPoolExecutor · docling
runs in-process and holds the GIL.
forkserver or spawn, never plain fork —
a forked child inherits a broken CUDA context.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
one 675-page document is 5% of the corpus's pages.
Picked up last it would define the wall clock by itself.
File size, not page count — counting pages needs a
PDF library the corpus layer refuses to depend on.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
init_worker — one CUDA card each
a shared counter under a lock, round-robin over
usable_devices() (≥ 2.5 GiB free). Without this,
docling's AcceleratorDevice.AUTO resolves to
cuda:0 in every process.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
the exception is returned, not raised, so both the value
and its type survive pickling — sync reports
ExtractionError and BackendUnavailable differently

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the parent keeps what only the parent can do
every ledger and cache write · results replayed in bib order
sqlite has a single writer, and the parent is the only place
that can order results deterministically

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
convert(raises_on_error=True) raises only on FAILURE.
A PARTIAL_SUCCESS would hand the citation gate a source that
silently ends at page k of n — so both call sites check the
status and raise before anything is written.

div.style: color: rgb(26, 26, 26) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
and around all of it: one writer at a time
content/pipeline.lock.db · a dedicated sqlite file under BEGIN IMMEDIATE
a RESERVED lock does not block readers, so the gate, retrieval and the
drafting skills keep working during a run. A second writer gets SQLITE_BUSY
and exits 2. A killed holder releases it immediately — no staleness heuristic.

svg.text: Level 5 — inside one parse: the worker pool, and everything that can go wrong
